gaps.sentence: Students ___ leave the examination room without permission.
gaps.explanation: Formal rules use 'may not' (or 'must not') to deny permission: may not leave.

gaps.sentence: The invoices ___ last week, so the delay is entirely our fault.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have + participle' criticises a past omission; passive adds 'been sent'.

gaps.sentence: The lights are on and I can hear the vacuum cleaner, so someone ___ be at home.
gaps.explanation: Evidence-based certainty uses 'must': must be at home.
'Would you like …?' is the standard polite offer.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ to hand in essays by Friday at the latest.
gaps.hint: ought to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' takes the full infinitive, so only 'ought' fits before 'to': ought.

gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.

gaps.sentence: You ___ seen the consultant's report — it is confidential and you have no clearance.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have + participle' expresses certainty that something did not happen.

gaps.sentence: You ___ decide now — take your time and think it over.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' removes the obligation to act immediately: needn't decide.
